Subject: POC execution sprint: success metrics, model pairing & owner Roster

Hi Elaine / Diego —

Thanks again for taking time earlier today. Quick recap and a proposed execution plan so we can kick the POC next week per your timeline. I tried to keep this tight so you can share internally.

POC goal (what success looks like)
- Business objective: reduce first-response time in chat flows and improve answer accuracy for payment reconciliation questions across EN/ES/PT.
- Acceptance criteria (minimum):
  - Precision on canonical reconciliation intents >= 88% (measured on your seed test set)
  - Latency p95 <= 700ms for 4k token context on Dedicated instance during synthetic traffic (scaled to expected 25 rps bursts)
  - Multilingual passing thresholds: EN >= 88%, ES >= 82%, PT >= 80%
  - No PII leak incidents; logs retained per your policy (30 days)

Model pairing suggestion (initial):
- Primary: Mistral-7B-Instruct (q4 quantized) — best balance for instruction-following across short/medium context and lower cost.
- Fallback / long-context: Llama-3-8B-qlora — better long-context stability for bank statement excerpts and long threads.
- Locale-specific tuning: evaluate small prompt templates per locale first, consider light fine-tune/rlf on your labeled 500 examples if needed.

Operational asks from LumenPay
- A seed test set (min 300 per language) with ground-truth labels for reconciliation intents and a few edge-case transcripts.
- Confirmation on data residency (you mentioned US-only) so we can provision a private Dedicated pool in us-west-2.
- Point of contact for legal to handle an expedited MSA review.

Timeline (proposed, 6-week sprint)
- Week 0 (kickoff): sign MSA + provision Dedicated instance (1 day provisioning once approved)
- Week 1: ingest seed test set, baseline eval on both models, smoke tests
- Week 2–3: iterate prompt templates, KV-cache tuning, batching profiles; run synthetic load tests
- Week 4: quantization validation, fallback routing tests, guardrail rules (safety prompts + regex filters)
- Week 5: acceptance run, collect metrics, triage failure modes
- Week 6: readout and handoff/playbook delivery

Owners (initial)
- Redwood Solutions: Olga Petrov (you) — primary SRE for kickoffs and acceptance criteria alignment
- Redwood Engineering: Marcus Lin — model pairing, quantization, performance tuning
- Customer Success: Stephanie Nguyen — onboarding, success metrics, readout
- LumenPay: Elaine Park (TPM) + Diego Morales (Engineering lead) — data, seed set, legal lane

Attachments: I attached a lightweight POC_success_metrics_template.xlsx and a model_pairing_note.pdf that explain the quantization tradeoffs and fallback routing we typically use.

Next steps (asks for this week)
1) Please confirm the acceptance criteria above (or flag changes).
2) Share the seed test set or a sample extract by Tue EOD so we can baseline.
3) Indicate legal contact for MSA; I attached a redlined starter to speed review.

If that all looks good I’ll book a 30-min kickoff for next Wed and get Marcus and Stephanie on the invite.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com

Quick engineering note — we’re good to move forward on the proposed pairing. A few technical points I’ll own during the sprint: 

1) Quantization profile: we’ll run q4_0 for Mistral-7B to get the cost/latency sweet spot and do an int8 validation pass if accuracy drops under threshold.
2) Fallback routing: implement a simple latency + confidence rule — if Mistral confidence < 0.6 OR response time > 800ms, route to Llama-3-8B-qlora for a second attempt. We’ll log both responses for acceptance gating.
3) Multilingual handling: we’ll maintain per-locale prompt templates and a light confidence calibration per language during Week 2.
4) Resource estimate: 1 dedicated 8-GPU pool for perf validation (we’ll scale down after acceptance).

I attached a short note (model_pairing_note.pdf) with the tradeoffs and the test commands we’ll run. I’ll start provisioning on Thu once legal clears the MSA.
